title: Odile and the Sigil Anew
premise: Edmund Quintana, the crown's food-taster, has spent years swallowing poison and memorizing smuggler roads through the Thornfell mountains to earn a quiet life. When the queen declares a purge of anyone bearing the old sigil-gift, Edmund discovers their own body carries it — awakened by every poison survived — and shelters a fugitive child who bears the sigil anew, a living key to a war the crown wants finished. Hunted by the inquisitor Wren Halloway, a former friend, Edmund must choose between the law that fed them and the mountain folk who remember what the sigil truly means. In the end, Edmund uses their immunity and road-knowledge to spirit the child beyond Thornfell's passes, publicly breaks the sigil's power rather than let either side weaponize it, and finds belonging not in crown or rebellion but among those who choose memory over vengeance.
about_author: Mara Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town court records before turning to fantasy. They write about people caught between institutions and the communities that outlast them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A routine tasting at the royal table goes wrong when Edmund detects poison no one else can smell — faster than training should allow. Establishes Edmund's careful, invisible life and their strange growing resistance. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, the first hint that Edmund's body is changing into something the crown would fear.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The queen's herald announces the Sigil Purge: all bearers of the old gift must register or be hunted. Edmund watches neighbors line up to denounce each other. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as Edmund realizes registering means testing — and testing will reveal them.

chapters.title: What the Poison Left
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, flashback-woven. Edmund examines the silver mark blooming on their wrist after years of swallowed toxins, remembering their grandmother's warnings about the sigil-gift. Emotional beat: grief and self-recognition; Edmund accepts they are what the proclamation hunts.

chapters.title: The Child in the Grain Cart
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Smuggling a private shipment through Thornfell, Edmund finds Ilsa, an eight-year-old stowaway with a burning sigil scar, fleeing inquisitors who burned her village. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion; Edmund cannot hand her back and knows it.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: POV Wren Halloway. The inquisitor — Edmund's childhood friend from the taster's quarters — arrives in Thornfell tracking sigil-bearers, efficient and quietly grieving her own registered brother. Emotional beat: Wren's conviction cracking at the edges; she suspects Edmund already.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund bargains with the fence Odile Vane for safe passage, trading secrets of the palace kitchens. Odile recognizes the sigil and names its price. Emotional beat: transactional trust forming; Edmund learns the mountain folk have kept sigil-memory alive in secret.

chapters.title: The Hollow Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Hidden in an abandoned chapel, Ilsa's sigil flares and shows Edmund fragments of the ancient war — the gift was never a weapon but a record-keeping magic, erased by the crown. Emotional beat: awe and anger; history itself becomes contraband.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren burns a registry village and keeps a ledger of names, telling herself order prevents worse bloodshed. She interrogates a survivor who knew Edmund's grandmother. Emotional beat: guilt rationalized; the hunt begins pointing toward Edmund.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund leads Ilsa along forgotten smuggler paths only they know, teaching her mountain survival while dodging patrols. Emotional beat: tentative belonging; Edmund becomes, without deciding to, a guardian.

chapters.title: The Queen's Table
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Summoned back to the capital, Edmund must taste for the queen while hiding Ilsa with Odile, and nearly faints as the poisons accelerate the sigil's growth. Emotional beat: terror under composure; the double life narrows.

chapters.title: Halloway's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren confronts Edmund privately: she knows, and offers falsified papers if Edmund surrenders the child. Emotional beat: betrayal and tenderness entangled; two loyalties demand the same body.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Odile reveals the mountain conclave can unmake the sigil — but the ritual requires a bearer willing to give it up willingly, and Ilsa is too young to choose. Emotional beat: moral weight shifting onto Edmund alone.

chapters.title: The Conclave Beneath Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In caverns lit by sigil-light, Edmund meets the last keepers, who show the full archive-magic: every bearer who died carried memories the crown destroyed. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into purpose; Edmund sees what ending the purge could restore.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren discovers her brother's name crossed out in an inquisitor's ledger — executed despite registration. Her certainty collapses. Emotional beat: disillusionment; the law she served was never just.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A frightened keeper sells the conclave's location to buy his family's safety. Inquisitors descend; Edmund and Ilsa flee through collapsing tunnels. Emotional beat: fury and heartbreak; even the persecuted betray under fear.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Searching the conclave ruins, Wren touches a surviving sigil-stone and receives a dead bearer's memory — her own grandmother, erased from family records. Emotional beat: shattering recognition; Wren crosses to the other side of the hunt.

chapters.title: The Siege of Vane's Hold
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Crown forces trap Edmund, Ilsa, and Odile at the hold. Edmund negotiates using knowledge of the kitchen's poison stores, buying hours at terrible cost. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity; Edmund spends their old life coin by coin.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cornered, Edmund chooses the ritual: they take Ilsa's sigil into their own body and then release it entirely, letting centuries of stored memory disperse into the mountain wind where no crown or army can claim it. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation; the secret dies so the people live.

chapters.title: Judgment
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren arrests the inquisitor-commander instead of Edmund, presenting her ledger of executions as evidence before the crown's own tribunal. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, costly and incomplete; Wren loses her rank and gains her name back.

chapters.title: After the Wind
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund, sigil-less and stripped of office, wakes in Odile's hold among mountain folk who simply set another place at the table. Emotional beat: quiet belonging; survival without glory.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Question
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Ilsa asks whether forgetting the sigil means the dead are lost forever. Edmund answers with stories, teaching her the oral memory the keepers preserved. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; memory outlives magic.

chapters.title: The Road Goes On
chapters.summary: POV Edmund and Wren alternating. Spring comes; Edmund guides refugees over the passes one last time, and Wren walks beside them as a free woman. Emotional beat: open-ended hope; the roads remember, and so do they.
